songs.name: Sitting On Top Of The World

ai_show_review.summary: High‑energy Dark Star suite, fiery Viola Lee Blues, tight jams
ai_show_review.blurb: The Ark show erupts in a seamless second‑set jam chain – Foxy Lady jam into Dark Star → Saint Stephen → The Eleven → Turn On Your Lovelight. Jerry’s guitar is on fire and the rhythm section drives the music forward. Highlights include a scorching Viola Lee Blues encore and a brilliant Cryptical Envelopment → The Other One sequence.
ai_show_review.review: On April 21, 1969 at Boston’s The Ark the Dead delivered one of their quintessential late‑'60s outings. After a rocky opening set that still yielded a powerful Morning Dew and a daring Cryptical Envelopment > The Other One sandwich, the second set launched into an unbroken improvisational tide: a wild Foxy Lady jam segues straight into a soaring Dark Star, which flows into Saint Stephen, then rockets through the manic time‑signature gymnastics of The Eleven before bursting into a jubilant Turn On Your Lovelight. The encore caps the night with a blistering Viola Lee Blues and an atmospheric feedback outro that leaves the audience buzzing. Across all six soundboard sources the recording quality is crystal clear – especially the Miller SBD (gd1969-04-21.sbd.miller.88465.sbeok.flac16) which captures every nuance without drop‑outs, making this the definitive version to hear.

best_recording.reason: Excellent sound‑board capture with pristine clarity, full set intact and no audible dropouts – showcases the legendary jam chain perfectly.

key_highlights: Dark Star → Saint Stephen → The Eleven → Turn On Your Lovelight suite
Viola Lee Blues encore with fiery Garcia leads
Foxy Lady jam that launches the second‑set improvisation
Cryptical Envelopment > The Other One sequence in Set 1

band_performance.Jerry: Garcia’s tone is described as rich and perfect; he rips through Dark Star, shreds on Viola Lee Blues, delivers inventive slide work on Hard To Handle, and provides gorgeous leads throughout the jams.
band_performance.Phil: Lesh’s bass is huge and bezerker‑mode on The Eleven, lays down big chords in Lovelight, and displays telepathic interplay with the rest of the band.
band_performance.Bob: Weir’s rhythm guitar holds steady; his vocal presence is clear but there are no specific standout moments noted.
band_performance.Mickey: Hart’s drumming is solid and powerful, contributing strong duo work with Bill throughout the improvisations.
band_performance.Billy: Kreutzmann provides a grooving, supportive foundation, locking in tightly with Hart for a dynamic rhythm section.

must_listen_sequences: Sitting On Top Of The World
